ideas.risks: The finite-prefix optimizer may still sacrifice old horizons in a way monotonicity cannot repair; the proof may collapse back to the already accepted fixed-envelope compactness criterion.
ideas.summary: Try to prove a market-specific gluing theorem: for deterministic exogenous known paths, D_n(P)=o(n) plus monotonicity of each suffix maximum M_{t,T} in T implies existence of one horizon-oblivious marginal sequence with o(T) regret. Focus on a scale-stability lemma showing finite-prefix solutions can be modified so all dyadic older horizons keep sublinear deficits.
ideas.title: Monotone Gluing From D_n
ideas.why_promising: This is the current sharp open target identified by the solver, and the abstract parity obstruction is not obviously realizable by monotone market suffix maxima.

ideas.risks: Market monotonicity may prevent the parity pattern entirely, or any attempted construction may make D_n linear and therefore fail to separate the criteria.
ideas.summary: Attempt a deterministic market path with D_n=o(n) but no fixed sublinear envelope, mimicking the solver's abstract parity obstruction. Use rapidly growing blocks whose finite-prefix optimizer alternates between incompatible quote distributions, then compute D_n and the fixed-envelope LP explicitly.
ideas.title: Market Parity Obstruction
ideas.why_promising: A successful example would settle that D_n=o(n) is not sufficient; a failed, well-analyzed attempt would reveal what extra monotone structure a gluing proof can exploit.

ideas.risks: The calculations may only confirm known easy behavior and not produce a theorem; stochastic versions introduce conditioning and measurability issues.
ideas.summary: Compute D_n(P), or tight upper/lower asymptotics, for the existing tail-bad but learnable examples: sparse vanishing spikes, power-of-two spikes, superexponential uniform spikes, coded-delay variants, and alternating paths. For each, produce explicit marginals and dual certificates.
ideas.title: D_n On Tail Counterexamples
ideas.why_promising: This tests whether D_n is the right decision-relevant replacement for beta/gamma/Delta tails and builds a regression suite for future characterization claims.

ideas.risks: The exact correction may depend on threshold-round ordering and strict-crossing conventions; the current O(m) slack may be unavoidable for arbitrary menus.
ideas.summary: Sharpen the solver's finite increasing-block estimate. For P=0^N,c_1,...,c_m, prove whether D_{N+m}=N kappa(C) exactly in the left-limit model, or identify the exact additive correction from the threshold-round actions. Start with m=3 and compare primal and dual LPs.
ideas.title: Exact Increasing-Block D_n
ideas.why_promising: It would make D_n concrete on the main lower-bound gadget and may expose the local algebra needed for global gluing or counterexamples.

ideas.risks: The stage payoffs may not decompose cleanly because V_T^* is horizon-level; infinite-dimensional closedness and norm choices may obscure rather than clarify the problem.
ideas.summary: Reformulate deterministic known-path anytime design as vector approachability of the negative orthant, with one coordinate per horizon deficit. Investigate whether infinite-dimensional, set-valued, or response-based approachability results give either a gluing theorem or a computable sufficient condition.
ideas.title: Approachability Formulation
ideas.why_promising: The problem is intrinsically one action sequence serving many horizon objectives, which is exactly the kind of simultaneous constraint geometry approachability was built to express.

ideas.risks: The resulting modulus may be tautological or no easier to verify than the fixed-envelope criterion; weighted duals may be technically messy.
ideas.summary: Define scale-sensitive finite-prefix moduli between D_n=o(n) and the fixed-envelope criterion, such as weighted LPs controlling deficit_T/e_T for all T<=n or dyadic-window values controlling all T in [alpha n,n]. Prove exact compactness equivalences and derive dual certificates.
ideas.title: Scale-Sensitive Prefix Moduli
ideas.why_promising: If D_n is too weak, this may yield a still-checkable characterization that avoids arbitrary envelope feasibility while blocking the solver's old-horizon sacrifice issue.

ideas.risks: Stable-comparator conditions may be only sufficient and far from necessary; switching quote levels can be subtle because old quotes remain active and single-fill censoring matters.
ideas.summary: Develop readable sufficient conditions based on the exact comparator V_T^*=sup_b b |{t<T:M_{t,T}>b}|. Examples: one quote b is o(T)-optimal for all large T, the optimal quote lies in a finite menu with few costly switches, or argmax drift is slow in a quantified value metric.
ideas.title: Stable Comparator Conditions
ideas.why_promising: It explains easy paths like alternating 1/2,1 and could provide useful structure below the full LP characterization.

ideas.risks: Law-aware horizon-specific pseudo-regret collapses if quantifiers are not fixed; conditional LPs require careful measurable selection and adaptation bookkeeping.
ideas.summary: Extend the deterministic finite-prefix LP to exogenous stochastic processes by using conditional payoff functions phi_{t,T}(a)=E[a 1{max_{t<s<=T}P_s>a}|F_t] and probability-weighted horizon deficits. Test rare-history constructions where essential sup tails are large but expected regret is small.
ideas.title: Conditional Stochastic D_n
ideas.why_promising: The original model allows stochastic prices; a conditional, probability-weighted modulus could connect deterministic path insights with expected-regret learnability while avoiding essential-sup false positives.

ideas.risks: This improves sufficiency rather than necessity; delayed-bandit results may not map cleanly to public-price full-information counterfactual rewards.
ideas.summary: Translate adaptive delayed-learning ideas based on skipped feedback, outstanding observations, or tracking capacity to the grid market-making reduction. Aim for regret bounds using payoff-weighted skipped mass or observed outstanding-fill complexity rather than a fixed known truncation H.
ideas.title: Adaptive Truncation Algorithms
ideas.why_promising: The literature consistently points away from raw elapsed-delay tails and toward missing-information quantities; this can strengthen the accepted if-direction under unknown tails.
